about: Havenbrooke's woods on foot (dungeon/hexes.py, requirements "### Hex crawl"): a hex crawl of one-mile hexes into the woods and hills west and south of Haven, entered from Ironroot Woods or the Riverwalk. No hexes are authored; the land is generated from the campaign seed and goes on as far as anyone walks. Trips between towns stay on Havenbrooke's roads (travel/havenbrooke.json). Walking eats nothing from the pack, as everywhere in Havenbrooke.

haven-woods.text: Two students from Warden Hall on a map-and-compass exercise, arguing about which way is west.
A hunter's tree stand, empty, with a thermos left on the seat and still warm.
An old stone wall running straight through the trees, from when all of this was farms.

haven-woods.action: keep footing on the wet leaves going down the gully
haven-woods.threat: The leaves go out from under the character halfway down the gully. Mud to the waist and a turned ankle.

haven-woods.action: notice the warding marks on the trees before crossing them
haven-woods.threat: The character walks through a coven's ward line without seeing it. Every hair stands up, and somebody, somewhere, now knows.

deep-woods.text: A clearing with a ring of flattened grass, as if something large sleeps here, and paw prints the size of a hand.
No phone signal, and the trees all look alike.

deep-woods.action: get out of the way of the pack running through

threat.text: Lycans on a run come through the trees fast and do not stop for anyone in the way.

deep-woods.action: leave the lights in the trees alone
deep-woods.threat: Small lights in the trees lead the character off the path and leave them in the dark, an hour from anywhere, with no idea how.

haven-woods.text: Coyotes yipping across the valley, and the lights of Haven far off below.

haven-woods.action: pick a dry spot before the rain

deep-woods.text: Howling, close, and then nothing at all until dawn.

deep-woods.action: wake before whatever is circling the camp comes in

threat.text: A feral lycan, alone and not right, comes into the firelight.

any.text: What is left of a farm the woods took back: a cellar hole, lilacs gone wild, a stone chimney standing on its own.
A camp people come back to: a fire ring, crushed cans, a tarp strung between trees and initials carved in a beech.
A clearing nobody stumbles on by accident: stones set in a ring, burnt herbs, and the feeling of being looked at.
A den dug under a rock ledge, the ground worn bare, bones of deer and something with a collar on it.
An old quarry tunnel into the hillside, gated once; the gate hangs open now and the air from it is cold.
